note: Single-participant (sub-01) proof that the reliability pipeline runs correctly end-to-end against real downloaded, preprocessed data. Not a population-level reliability claim -- that requires all 20 participants, deferred to a controlled research workflow outside this session per the task's own CI/full-run distinction. An earlier version of session_reliability() grouped by 'condition' (perception/imagery, only 2 values), which gives a Pearson correlation that is trivially +-1 for any data with exactly 2 points; fixed to group by (condition, stimulus_id) instead (54 possible groups), which is what produced the non-trivial values below.

precue_vs_postcue_effect_size.interpretation: Posterior alpha and posterior ERP amplitude show a real post-cue vs pre-cue effect, consistent with stimulus-locked visual processing concentrated in occipital/posterior channels; frontal beta shows essentially none, as expected for a channel/band pair with no obvious visual-evoked relationship.

signal_quality_vs_target_correlation.interpretation: Near zero: a pure signal-quality proxy does not spuriously predict the vividness behavioral target for this participant, reducing (not eliminating) concern that a later H2 result could be driven by signal-quality confounds rather than content-relevant neural information.

preprocessing_qc_summary.note: See results/c1_preprocessing_qc.json for the full QC report, including the block_order_confound_flag=true finding that must be accounted for before any confirmatory H2/H3 claim.
